say.en: Tungsten filaments glow white-hot without melting, yet mercury is a liquid at room temperature. Both are d-block metals. The number of d electrons in bonding makes the difference. In this lesson: Explain the high melting points of transition metals.
Describe trends in atomic size and the lanthanoid contraction.
Explain irregular trends in ionisation enthalpy.

body.en: Nearly all transition elements are hard, lustrous metals with high tensile strength, conductivity and melting points. Both ns and (n−1)d electrons take part in *metallic* bonding, so the enthalpy of atomisation is high. Melting points rise to a maximum near the middle of each series (about d⁵) and then fall, because the number of unpaired electrons first rises and then falls. Zn, Cd and Hg, with full d sets, melt at low temperatures.
body.kn: ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹಗಳು ಗಟ್ಟಿ, ಹೊಳಪಿನ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದ್ರವನಬಿಂದುವಿನ ಲೋಹಗಳು. ns ಮತ್ತು (n−1)d ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳೆರಡೂ ಲೋಹೀಯ ಬಂಧದಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾಗವಹಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: On the board: trends across the 3d series

say.en: Melting points rise to a peak near vanadium and chromium, where many unpaired d electrons join the metallic bonding, then fall to zinc.
Atomic radii fall across the series and then level off. The 4d and 5d metals are almost the same size because of the lanthanoid contraction.
Ionisation enthalpy rises slowly. Jumps appear where a stable d¹⁰ or d⁵ ion would be broken.

text.en: IE₂ of Cu high: Cu⁺ is d¹⁰
IE₃ of Mn high: Mn²⁺ is d⁵

say.en: Density rises from scandium to copper as size falls and mass grows.

body.en: Across a series the atomic radius decreases slowly, because each new electron enters an inner d orbital and shields the growing nuclear charge fairly well. Going down, 4d atoms are larger than 3d atoms, but 5d atoms are almost the same size as 4d atoms (Zr 160 pm, Hf 159 pm). This is due to the lanthanoid contraction: the 4f electrons that fill before the 5d series shield poorly. *Ionisation* enthalpies rise slowly and irregularly across a series; breaking a stable d⁵ or d¹⁰ set needs extra energy, so Cr and Cu have high second, and Mn high third, ionisation enthalpies.
body.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಮಾಣು ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಲ್ಯಾಂಥನಾಯ್ಡ್ ಸಂಕೋಚನದಿಂದ 4d ಮತ್ತು 5d ಧಾತುಗಳ ಗಾತ್ರ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಸಮಾನ. ಸ್ಥಿರ d⁵ ಅಥವಾ d¹⁰ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ಮುರಿಯಲು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಬೇಕು.

problem.en: Use configurations to explain why the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu is higher than that of Zn, while the first ionisation enthalpy of Zn is higher than that of Cu.

steps.en: Cu: 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ → Cu⁺: 3d¹⁰. The second electron must come out of the full 3d¹⁰ set: about 1958 kJ mol⁻¹.
Zn: 3d¹⁰ 4s² → Zn⁺: 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. The second electron is the lone 4s electron, leaving stable 3d¹⁰: about 1734 kJ mol⁻¹.
For the first electron, Zn removes it from a filled 4s² pair with a higher nuclear charge (30 vs 29), so Zn's first value is higher.

answer.en: IE₂: Cu > Zn because Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰; IE₁: Zn > Cu

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Use configurations to explain why the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu is higher than that of Zn, while the first ionisation enthalpy of Zn is higher than that of Cu.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Use configurations to explain why the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu is higher than that of Zn, while the first ionisation enthalpy of Zn is higher than that of Cu.
Cu: 3d to the power 10 4s to the power 1 gives Cu⁺: 3d to the power 10. The second electron must come out of the full 3d to the power 10 set: about 1958 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.

Zn: 3d to the power 10 4 square seconds gives Zn⁺: 3d to the power 10 4s to the power 1. The second electron is the lone 4 seconds electron, leaving stable 3d to the power 10: about 1734 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
For the first electron, Zn removes it from a filled 4 square seconds pair with a higher nuclear charge 30 vs 29, so Zn's first value is higher.
So the answer is IE 2: Cu is greater than Zn because Cu⁺ is 3d to the power 10; IE 1: Zn is greater than Cu.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. Which 3d metal has the lowest melting point?
Zn (3d to the power 10 4 square seconds) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so its melting point (about 420 degrees Celsius) is the lowest in the 3d series.
